key_developments.event: Francis and 11 companions receive oral approval from Innocent III.
Clare of Assisi founds the Second Order (Poor Clares).
Final rule (Regula bullata) confirmed by Honorius III.
John XXII condemns the Spiritual Franciscan position on apostolic poverty.

_quarry.description: Founded by Francis of Assisi in 1209 and approved orally by Pope Innocent III, the Franciscans were a radical experiment in apostolic poverty — friars who owned nothing, individually or collectively, and survived by begging. Tension between the founder's strict ideal and the order's rapid institutional growth produced the Spiritual/Conventual split (1270s+). Franciscans rivalled the Dominicans in the universities (Bonaventure, Duns Scotus, William of Ockham).
